tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

2	
3	## What the code does today (facts, checked 2026-10-30)
4	
5	- 燃烧瓶投掷者 (`thrower`) lobs a bottle; its fire lasts `fire_time` 3.0 s
6	  (`game/enemy_attacks.gd:34`), 0 when the thrower is silenced
7	  (`entities/enemy.gd:1200`). Throwers spawn in the city region
8	  (`game/enemy_attacks.gd:163`).
9	- The bottle lands after 0.6 s (`entities/molotov.gd:8`) and calls
10	  `game.spawn_hazard(at, radius, 0.0, fire_time, …)` (`entities/molotov.gd:67`,
11	  `game/game_manager.gd:794`): a `GroundHazard` with `fuse` 0 and `lasting` 3.0.
12	- `GroundHazard` counts `lasting` down by the physics delta in
13	  `_physics_process`, only while `game.simulation_active()` is true
14	  (`entities/ground_hazard.gd:62`, `game/game_manager.gd:386`), hits every
15	  0.5 s, and frees itself when `lasting` reaches 0.
16	- The fire on the ground today is a `Decal` with a code-made circle texture
17	  (`entities/ground_hazard.gd:31`). A Decal takes textures, not a shader, so

34	## The state
35	
36	- What it communicates, and why the player needs it: 传达“这片地面仍会造成周期伤害，以及还剩多少燃烧时间”。玩家据此决定绕行还是等待；亮黄火焰逐渐转成暗红余烬并减弱，消失才表示这堆火的持续伤害结束。暗淡不表示已安全。
37	- Name of the state: `fire_patch_burning`，成立条件为 `fuse <= 0.0 && lasting > 0.0`。当前投掷瓶火堆生成即成立；虫子爆炸和 Boss last rite 的 `lasting == 0`，不属于该状态。
38	- Script and variable that hold it: `entities/ground_hazard.gd` 的 `fuse`、`lasting`；`game.simulation_active()` 决定倒计时是否推进。未来显示驱动在有效火堆生成、第一次物理倒计时之前缓存该实例的初始 `lasting` 为 `initial_lasting`，之后只读状态并写材质：`fire_remaining = clamp(lasting / initial_lasting, 0.0, 1.0)`。不硬编码分母 3.0，因此未来改变 `fire_time` 仍能归一化。初始值不大于 0 的危险区不创建火焰，也不做除法。

40	## Effect specification
41	
42	### The shader
43	
44	- Path: `res://shaders/burning_bottle_fire.gdshader`（本次只约定路径，不创建 shader）。
45	- `shader_type`: `spatial`，火焰是三维场景中 `MeshInstance3D` 的材质。
46	- `render_mode`: `unshaded, blend_add, cull_disabled, depth_draw_never, shadows_disabled, fog_disabled`。
47	
48	`unshaded` 使火色不依赖灯光；`blend_add` 在线性空间把火光加到背景上；
49	`cull_disabled` 防止观察角度变化时面片背面消失；`depth_draw_never` 避免透明面片写深度；
50	`shadows_disabled` 和 `fog_disabled` 避免接收阴影、雾的衰减。
51	另外把 mesh 的 `cast_shadow` 设为 OFF（`shadows_disabled` 本身不禁止投影），
52	保留正常深度测试，让实体墙壁仍可遮挡火焰。
53	
54	显示结构：每个有效火堆增加一个朝向相机的面片，宽 `2 * radius`、高 `1.6 * radius`，
55	底部在地面上方 0.04 世界单位；与原有 Decal 共存。无贴图采样、无 `sampler2D`。
56	
57	| Uniform | Type | Hint | Default | Set by |
58	|---|---|---|---|---|
59	| fire_remaining | float | `hint_range(0.0, 1.0, 0.01)` | `1.0` | driver, from the state |
60	| hot_color | vec4 | `source_color` | `vec4(1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0)` | material default（不改） |
61	| ember_color | vec4 | `source_color` | `vec4(1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0)` | material default（不改） |
62	| intensity | float | `hint_range(0.0, 1.0, 0.01)` | `0.6` | material default（不改） |
63	| flicker_amount | float | `hint_range(0.0, 0.2, 0.01)` | `0.08` | material default；受控截图显式设 `0.0` |
64	
65	数值 hint 用于检视器，不代替驱动中的 clamp。颜色的 RGB 按 `source_color` 的颜色语义处理，
66	alpha 不作 sRGB 解码；本方案两种默认颜色的 RGB 只有 0 和 1，解码前后数值相同。
67	
68	### The colour line
69	
70	```glsl
71	ALBEDO = mix(ember_color.rgb, hot_color.rgb, fire_remaining) * intensity;
72	```
73	
74	后续 shader 必须逐字使用上面这条颜色语句。它给出线性火色；透明度另由形状和剩余比例决定。
75	为固定可计算的形状，约定中间量如下（这里只写数学定义，不是已实现的 shader）：
76	
77	- `p = 2 * UV - 1`；先令 `p.x *= 1 + 1.5 * max(-p.y, 0)`，使顶部收窄。
78	- 再令 `p.x += flicker_amount * sin(8 * UV.y + 7 * TIME) * (1 - UV.y)`，使上部摆动
79	  （Godot 的 UV.y 在面片顶部为 0、底部为 1，所以用 `1 - UV.y` 让顶部摆幅最大、底部不动）。
80	- `shape = clamp(1 - dot(p, p), 0, 1)`；`flicker = 1 + flicker_amount * sin(11 * TIME)`。
81	- `ALPHA = clamp(shape * clamp(fire_remaining, 0, 1) * flicker, 0, 1)`。
82	
83	颜色 uniform 的 alpha 不参与上述计算；截图只改 `flicker_amount=0`，不临时替换颜色那一行。

282	## Questions
283	
284	1. **Which renderer does `project.godot` name, and what does it rule out?** 文件没有显式写 rendering_method，只指定 Windows 的 `d3d12` 驱动（`project.godot:27`）；桌面缺省是 Forward+，本次运行也确认为 forward_plus/d3d12。D3D12 是图形驱动而不是第四种 renderer。作业列出的限制是：Decal 和 compute shader 需要 Forward+ 或 Mobile；VoxelGI、SDFGI、SSIL 在 Mobile 和 Compatibility 下不可用。Forward+ 不排除其中任何一项。这对本项目是实际约束：火堆的地面烧痕是 Decal（`entities/ground_hazard.gd:31`），基地环境开着 SSIL（`game/game_manager.gd:6550`，`base_environment()` 里的 `e.ssil_enabled = true`）。换成 Compatibility 会两样都失去，换成 Mobile 会失去 SSIL。颜色管线的预测也只在 Forward+/Mobile 下成立。依据：[Godot Overview of renderers](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/rendering/renderers.html)。
285	2. **What colour arrives in `fragment()` before you change it, and what would the tempting alternative give you?** 本例是 spatial，不存在 canvas_item 自动把默认纹理颜色乘入 COLOR 的语义。fragment 收到的 COLOR 是从 vertex 阶段传来的插值顶点颜色；普通 QuadMesh 未提供顶点色时为白色。直接 `ALBEDO=COLOR.rgb` 会得到白色自发亮面片（本例 unshaded），不会自动得到火焰或贴图颜色。`texture(albedo_tex,UV).rgb` 才是显式纹理采样，颜色 sampler 还需 source_color；无纹理火 shader 不使用它。依据：[Godot Spatial shaders — built-ins](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/shaders/shader_reference/spatial_shader.html#built-ins)。
286	3. **Spatial: what does `ALBEDO` hold if you never write it, and what does `COLOR` hold?** ALBEDO 默认是白色 vec3(1.0)；它是输出，不是自动采好的颜色贴图。COLOR 是顶点颜色传入 fragment 的值；当前 QuadMesh 无自定义顶点色，所以为 vec4(1.0)。两者不自动等价，必须显式写 ALBEDO 才能使用所需的颜色。依据：同上 Spatial shaders 的 ALBEDO 与 COLOR 条目。
287	4. **How long would a frame-counting version last at 30, 60 and 144 fps?** 按 60 fps 的 3 秒定为 `N=3*60=180` 帧，若每渲染帧减 1，则 30 fps 为 `180/30=6.0 s`、60 fps 为 `180/60=3.0 s`、144 fps 为 `180/144=1.25 s`。若错误计数发生在物理回调，则应把分母换成物理频率，不能把显示 fps 当物理频率。
288	5. **Which resource holds the uniform's default, which its current value, and what happens if two objects share the material?** 默认声明存于 Shader 源码；ShaderMaterial 保存该材质的当前覆盖值，未覆盖时回退到 Shader 默认值。两个 mesh 共享同一个 ShaderMaterial 时，set_shader_parameter 改的是同一份覆盖值，两个对象一起改变；本计划 R7 共享 Shader、各自 new 材质，所以寿命比例独立。依据：[Godot ShaderMaterial](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_shadermaterial.html)。
289	6. **Does `hint_range` clamp a value the driver sets from code? (Predict now.)** 预测不会；它约束检视器控件，不会自动替代码 clamp。实现后在独立校准材质上用代码设 fire_remaining=2.0，先停驱动覆盖，再断言 get_shader_parameter 返回 2.0，并截图对照。颜色那一行没有 clamp，mix 外插为 `(0.6,1.2,0)`；ALPHA 的显式 clamp 仍给 1，A 点预测 RGB8=(210,255,67)，区别于 r=1 的 (210,210,67)。这是越界实验，正常驱动仍把状态比例 clamp 到 [0,1]。现在是预测，尚未声称通过实测。依据：[Godot Shading language — Uniform hints](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/shaders/shader_reference/shading_language.html#uniform-hints)。

34	## The state
35	
36	- What it communicates, and why the player needs it: 传达“这片地面仍会造成周期伤害，以及还剩多少燃烧时间”。玩家据此决定绕行还是等待；亮黄火焰逐渐转成暗红余烬并减弱，消失才表示这堆火的持续伤害结束。暗淡不表示已安全。
37	- Name of the state: `fire_patch_burning`，成立条件为 `fuse <= 0.0 && lasting > 0.0`。当前投掷瓶火堆生成即成立；虫子爆炸和 Boss last rite 的 `lasting == 0`，不属于该状态。
38	- Script and variable that hold it: `entities/ground_hazard.gd` 的 `fuse`、`lasting`；`game.simulation_active()` 决定倒计时是否推进。未来显示驱动在有效火堆生成、第一次物理倒计时之前缓存该实例的初始 `lasting` 为 `initial_lasting`，之后只读状态并写材质：`fire_remaining = clamp(lasting / initial_lasting, 0.0, 1.0)`。不硬编码分母 3.0，因此未来改变 `fire_time` 仍能归一化。初始值不大于 0 的危险区不创建火焰，也不做除法。

40	## Effect specification
41	
42	### The shader
43	
44	- Path: `res://shaders/burning_bottle_fire.gdshader`（本次只约定路径，不创建 shader）。
45	- `shader_type`: `spatial`，火焰是三维场景中 `MeshInstance3D` 的材质。
46	- `render_mode`: `unshaded, blend_add, cull_disabled, depth_draw_never, shadows_disabled, fog_disabled`。
47	
48	`unshaded` 使火色不依赖灯光；`blend_add` 在线性空间把火光加到背景上；
49	`cull_disabled` 防止观察角度变化时面片背面消失；`depth_draw_never` 避免透明面片写深度；
50	`shadows_disabled` 和 `fog_disabled` 避免接收阴影、雾的衰减。
51	另外把 mesh 的 `cast_shadow` 设为 OFF（`shadows_disabled` 本身不禁止投影），
52	保留正常深度测试，让实体墙壁仍可遮挡火焰。
53	
54	显示结构：每个有效火堆增加一个朝向相机的面片，宽 `2 * radius`、高 `1.6 * radius`，
55	底部在地面上方 0.04 世界单位；与原有 Decal 共存。无贴图采样、无 `sampler2D`。
56	
57	| Uniform | Type | Hint | Default | Set by |
58	|---|---|---|---|---|
59	| fire_remaining | float | `hint_range(0.0, 1.0, 0.01)` | `1.0` | driver, from the state |
60	| hot_color | vec4 | `source_color` | `vec4(1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0)` | material default（不改） |
61	| ember_color | vec4 | `source_color` | `vec4(1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0)` | material default（不改） |
62	| intensity | float | `hint_range(0.0, 1.0, 0.01)` | `0.6` | material default（不改） |
63	| flicker_amount | float | `hint_range(0.0, 0.2, 0.01)` | `0.08` | material default；受控截图显式设 `0.0` |
64	
65	数值 hint 用于检视器，不代替驱动中的 clamp。颜色的 RGB 按 `source_color` 的颜色语义处理，
66	alpha 不作 sRGB 解码；本方案两种默认颜色的 RGB 只有 0 和 1，解码前后数值相同。
67	
68	### The colour line
69	
70	```glsl
71	ALBEDO = mix(ember_color.rgb, hot_color.rgb, fire_remaining) * intensity;
72	```
73	
74	后续 shader 必须逐字使用上面这条颜色语句。它给出线性火色；透明度另由形状和剩余比例决定。
75	为固定可计算的形状，约定中间量如下（这里只写数学定义，不是已实现的 shader）：
76	
77	- `p = 2 * UV - 1`；先令 `p.x *= 1 + 1.5 * max(-p.y, 0)`，使顶部收窄。
78	- 再令 `p.x += flicker_amount * sin(8 * UV.y + 7 * TIME) * (1 - UV.y)`，使上部摆动
79	  （Godot 的 UV.y 在面片顶部为 0、底部为 1，所以用 `1 - UV.y` 让顶部摆幅最大、底部不动）。
80	- `shape = clamp(1 - dot(p, p), 0, 1)`；`flicker = 1 + flicker_amount * sin(11 * TIME)`。
81	- `ALPHA = clamp(shape * clamp(fire_remaining, 0, 1) * flicker, 0, 1)`。
82	
83	颜色 uniform 的 alpha 不参与上述计算；截图只改 `flicker_amount=0`，不临时替换颜色那一行。

282	## Questions
283	
284	1. **Which renderer does `project.godot` name, and what does it rule out?** 文件没有显式写 rendering_method，只指定 Windows 的 `d3d12` 驱动（`project.godot:27`）；桌面缺省是 Forward+，本次运行也确认为 forward_plus/d3d12。D3D12 是图形驱动而不是第四种 renderer。作业列出的限制是：Decal 和 compute shader 需要 Forward+ 或 Mobile；VoxelGI、SDFGI、SSIL 在 Mobile 和 Compatibility 下不可用。Forward+ 不排除其中任何一项。这对本项目是实际约束：火堆的地面烧痕是 Decal（`entities/ground_hazard.gd:31`），基地环境开着 SSIL（`game/game_manager.gd:6550`，`base_environment()` 里的 `e.ssil_enabled = true`）。换成 Compatibility 会两样都失去，换成 Mobile 会失去 SSIL。颜色管线的预测也只在 Forward+/Mobile 下成立。依据：[Godot Overview of renderers](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/rendering/renderers.html)。
285	2. **What colour arrives in `fragment()` before you change it, and what would the tempting alternative give you?** 本例是 spatial，不存在 canvas_item 自动把默认纹理颜色乘入 COLOR 的语义。fragment 收到的 COLOR 是从 vertex 阶段传来的插值顶点颜色；普通 QuadMesh 未提供顶点色时为白色。直接 `ALBEDO=COLOR.rgb` 会得到白色自发亮面片（本例 unshaded），不会自动得到火焰或贴图颜色。`texture(albedo_tex,UV).rgb` 才是显式纹理采样，颜色 sampler 还需 source_color；无纹理火 shader 不使用它。依据：[Godot Spatial shaders — built-ins](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/shaders/shader_reference/spatial_shader.html#built-ins)。
286	3. **Spatial: what does `ALBEDO` hold if you never write it, and what does `COLOR` hold?** ALBEDO 默认是白色 vec3(1.0)；它是输出，不是自动采好的颜色贴图。COLOR 是顶点颜色传入 fragment 的值；当前 QuadMesh 无自定义顶点色，所以为 vec4(1.0)。两者不自动等价，必须显式写 ALBEDO 才能使用所需的颜色。依据：同上 Spatial shaders 的 ALBEDO 与 COLOR 条目。
287	4. **How long would a frame-counting version last at 30, 60 and 144 fps?** 按 60 fps 的 3 秒定为 `N=3*60=180` 帧，若每渲染帧减 1，则 30 fps 为 `180/30=6.0 s`、60 fps 为 `180/60=3.0 s`、144 fps 为 `180/144=1.25 s`。若错误计数发生在物理回调，则应把分母换成物理频率，不能把显示 fps 当物理频率。
288	5. **Which resource holds the uniform's default, which its current value, and what happens if two objects share the material?** 默认声明存于 Shader 源码；ShaderMaterial 保存该材质的当前覆盖值，未覆盖时回退到 Shader 默认值。两个 mesh 共享同一个 ShaderMaterial 时，set_shader_parameter 改的是同一份覆盖值，两个对象一起改变；本计划 R7 共享 Shader、各自 new 材质，所以寿命比例独立。依据：[Godot ShaderMaterial](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_shadermaterial.html)。
289	6. **Does `hint_range` clamp a value the driver sets from code? (Predict now.)** 预测不会；它约束检视器控件，不会自动替代码 clamp。实现后在独立校准材质上用代码设 fire_remaining=2.0，先停驱动覆盖，再断言 get_shader_parameter 返回 2.0，并截图对照。颜色那一行没有 clamp，mix 外插为 `(0.6,1.2,0)`；ALPHA 的显式 clamp 仍给 1，A 点预测 RGB8=(210,255,67)，区别于 r=1 的 (210,210,67)。这是越界实验，正常驱动仍把状态比例 clamp 到 [0,1]。现在是预测，尚未声称通过实测。依据：[Godot Shading language — Uniform hints](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/shaders/shader_reference/shading_language.html#uniform-hints)。

1	class_name GroundHazard
2	extends Node3D
3	
4	## A patch of ground that hurts (装备扩充策划案 §2.1, §7): a burning bottle's
5	## fire, the red circle before a volatile slug bursts. `fuse` seconds of warning
6	## first; then either one burst (`lasting` 0) or a tick every TICK seconds for
7	## `lasting` seconds. Hits Lappland inside it, and other enemies too when
8	## `hurts_enemies` (高能源石虫's blast is 敌我都伤).
9	
10	const TICK := 0.5
11	
12	var game: GameManager
13	var radius := 1.3
14	var fuse := 0.0
15	var lasting := 0.0
16	## Damage per burst, or per tick while it lasts.
17	var damage := 100.0
18	var kind := "arts"
19	var hurts_enemies := false
20	var source: Enemy
21	var colour := Color(1.0, 0.45, 0.15, 0.35)
22	var _tick := 0.0
23	var _burst_done := false
24	var _disc: Decal
25	
26	func _ready() -> void:
27		game = get_parent() as GameManager
28		add_to_group("ground_hazards")
29		# Projected down onto the ground so it follows a ramp; a flat disc sank
30		# into the uphill half there (用户 2026-10-22: 变成半圆).
31		_disc = Decal.new()
32		_disc.size = Vector3(radius * 2.0, clampf(radius * 1.2, 1.2, 3.0), radius * 2.0)
33		# Ground and props only, not the sprites standing in it.
34		_disc.cull_mask = 1
35		_disc.texture_albedo = _circle_texture()
36		_disc.texture_emission = _circle_texture(true)
37		_disc.emission_energy = 0.4
38		_disc.modulate = colour if fuse <= 0.0 else Color(0.95, 0.2, 0.15, 0.3)
39		add_child(_disc)
40		if fuse > 0.0:
41			# The fuse is a warning like any other: see-through red with rings
42			# counting down to the burst (新敌人攻击案 v1.2).
43			_disc.visible = false
44			var warning := CombatMarker.create("circle", Vector2(radius, 0.0), fuse)
45			warning.name = "Warning"
46			add_child(warning)
47			warning.position.y = 0.06
48	
49	static var _circles := {}
50	## A white disc with a soft one-texel rim, tinted by the decal. The emission
51	## copy is black outside instead of clear: decal emission ignores alpha.
52	static func _circle_texture(glow: bool = false) -> ImageTexture:
53		if _circles.has(glow): return _circles[glow]
54		var image := Image.create(64, 64, false, Image.FORMAT_RGBA8)
55		for y in range(64):
56			for x in range(64):
57				var a := clampf(32.0 - Vector2(x + 0.5 - 32.0, y + 0.5 - 32.0).length(), 0.0, 1.0)
58				image.set_pixel(x, y, Color(a, a, a, 1.0) if glow else Color(1, 1, 1, a))
59		_circles[glow] = ImageTexture.create_from_image(image)
60		return _circles[glow]
61	
62	func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
63		if not is_instance_valid(game) or not game.simulation_active(): return
64		if fuse > 0.0:
65			fuse -= delta
66			if fuse > 0.0: return
67			_disc.modulate = colour
68			_disc.visible = true
69			if lasting <= 0.0:
70				_hit_everything()
71				queue_free()
72				return
73		lasting -= delta
74		_tick -= delta
75		if _tick <= 0.0:
76			_tick = TICK
77			_hit_everything()
78		if lasting <= 0.0: queue_free()
79	
80	func _hit_everything() -> void:
81		if lasting <= 0.0 and not _burst_done:
82			_burst_done = true
83			CombatVfx.spawn(game, Vector3(global_position.x, game.ground_y(global_position) + 0.09, global_position.z), Vector3.FORWARD, "burst", 0, true)
84		if is_instance_valid(game.player) and _flat(game.player.global_position) <= radius:
85			game.player.take_damage(damage, kind, source if is_instance_valid(source) else null)
86		if not hurts_enemies: return
87		for node in get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("enemies"):
88			var enemy := node as Enemy
89			if enemy == null or enemy.game != game or enemy._dead or enemy == source: continue
90			if _flat(enemy.global_position) <= radius: enemy.take_hit(damage, kind)
91	
92	func _flat(point: Vector3) -> float:
93		return Vector2(point.x - global_position.x, point.z - global_position.z).length()

26	var _shadow: MeshInstance3D

42		if not is_instance_valid(game) or not game.simulation_active(): return
43		age += delta
44		if age >= FLIGHT:
45			_land()
46			return

50		var t := clampf(age / FLIGHT, 0.0, 1.0)
51		var ground := start.lerp(target, t)
52		ground.y = game.ground_y(ground)
53		var height := lerpf(start.y - game.ground_y(start), 0.0, t) + APEX * 4.0 * t * (1.0 - t)

55		_bottle.rotation.z = t * TAU * 1.5

1	class_name GroundHazard
2	extends Node3D
3	
4	## A patch of ground that hurts (装备扩充策划案 §2.1, §7): a burning bottle's
5	## fire, the red circle before a volatile slug bursts. `fuse` seconds of warning
6	## first; then either one burst (`lasting` 0) or a tick every TICK seconds for
7	## `lasting` seconds. Hits Lappland inside it, and other enemies too when
8	## `hurts_enemies` (高能源石虫's blast is 敌我都伤).
9	
10	const TICK := 0.5
11	
12	var game: GameManager
13	var radius := 1.3
14	var fuse := 0.0
15	var lasting := 0.0
16	## Damage per burst, or per tick while it lasts.
17	var damage := 100.0
18	var kind := "arts"
19	var hurts_enemies := false
20	var source: Enemy
21	var colour := Color(1.0, 0.45, 0.15, 0.35)
22	var _tick := 0.0
23	var _burst_done := false
24	var _disc: Decal
25	
26	func _ready() -> void:
27		game = get_parent() as GameManager
28		add_to_group("ground_hazards")
29		# Projected down onto the ground so it follows a ramp; a flat disc sank
30		# into the uphill half there (用户 2026-10-22: 变成半圆).
31		_disc = Decal.new()
32		_disc.size = Vector3(radius * 2.0, clampf(radius * 1.2, 1.2, 3.0), radius * 2.0)
33		# Ground and props only, not the sprites standing in it.
34		_disc.cull_mask = 1
35		_disc.texture_albedo = _circle_texture()
36		_disc.texture_emission = _circle_texture(true)
37		_disc.emission_energy = 0.4
38		_disc.modulate = colour if fuse <= 0.0 else Color(0.95, 0.2, 0.15, 0.3)
39		add_child(_disc)
40		if fuse > 0.0:
41			# The fuse is a warning like any other: see-through red with rings
42			# counting down to the burst (新敌人攻击案 v1.2).
43			_disc.visible = false
44			var warning := CombatMarker.create("circle", Vector2(radius, 0.0), fuse)
45			warning.name = "Warning"
46			add_child(warning)
47			warning.position.y = 0.06
48	
49	static var _circles := {}
50	## A white disc with a soft one-texel rim, tinted by the decal. The emission
51	## copy is black outside instead of clear: decal emission ignores alpha.
52	static func _circle_texture(glow: bool = false) -> ImageTexture:
53		if _circles.has(glow): return _circles[glow]
54		var image := Image.create(64, 64, false, Image.FORMAT_RGBA8)
55		for y in range(64):
56			for x in range(64):
57				var a := clampf(32.0 - Vector2(x + 0.5 - 32.0, y + 0.5 - 32.0).length(), 0.0, 1.0)
58				image.set_pixel(x, y, Color(a, a, a, 1.0) if glow else Color(1, 1, 1, a))
59		_circles[glow] = ImageTexture.create_from_image(image)
60		return _circles[glow]
61	
62	func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
63		if not is_instance_valid(game) or not game.simulation_active(): return
64		if fuse > 0.0:
65			fuse -= delta
66			if fuse > 0.0: return
67			_disc.modulate = colour
68			_disc.visible = true
69			if lasting <= 0.0:
70				_hit_everything()
71				queue_free()
72				return
73		lasting -= delta
74		_tick -= delta
75		if _tick <= 0.0:
76			_tick = TICK
77			_hit_everything()
78		if lasting <= 0.0: queue_free()
79	
80	func _hit_everything() -> void:
81		if lasting <= 0.0 and not _burst_done:
82			_burst_done = true
83			CombatVfx.spawn(game, Vector3(global_position.x, game.ground_y(global_position) + 0.09, global_position.z), Vector3.FORWARD, "burst", 0, true)
84		if is_instance_valid(game.player) and _flat(game.player.global_position) <= radius:
85			game.player.take_damage(damage, kind, source if is_instance_valid(source) else null)
86		if not hurts_enemies: return
87		for node in get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("enemies"):
88			var enemy := node as Enemy
89			if enemy == null or enemy.game != game or enemy._dead or enemy == source: continue
90			if _flat(enemy.global_position) <= radius: enemy.take_hit(damage, kind)

42		if not is_instance_valid(game) or not game.simulation_active(): return
43		age += delta
44		if age >= FLIGHT:
45			_land()
46			return

51		var ground := start.lerp(target, t)

53		var height := lerpf(start.y - game.ground_y(start), 0.0, t) + APEX * 4.0 * t * (1.0 - t)

6615		texture.gradient = gradient

930	## Shared with SceneDressing: a kit glb's mesh, every baked texture drawn
931	## through kit_piece.gdshader. Cached per path and gain.
932	static var _kit_cache := {}
933	static func kit_mesh(scene: PackedScene, gain: float = 1.0, snow_bias: float = 0.0) -> Mesh:
934		var key := "%s@%.2f@%.2f" % [scene.resource_path, gain, snow_bias]
935		if _kit_cache.has(key): return _kit_cache[key]
936		var mesh := _first_mesh(scene.instantiate())
937		if mesh == null: return mesh
938		mesh = mesh.duplicate()
939		for surface in range(mesh.get_surface_count()):
940			var source := mesh.surface_get_material(surface) as BaseMaterial3D
941			var material := ShaderMaterial.new()
942			material.shader = KIT_SHADER
943			# A part baked as "<piece>_glow" is a lamp's glass: drawn self-lit (a
944			# rebuilt piece exports it as "<piece>_glow.001": the suffix is dropped).
945			if source != null and source.resource_name.get_slice(".", 0).ends_with("_glow"):
946				material.shader = GLOW_SHADER
947			if source != null: material.set_shader_parameter("albedo_tex", source.albedo_texture)
948			# The relief baked with the colour (场景渲染统一改造案_v1 S2); the lit base shader reads it.
949			if source != null and source.normal_enabled and source.normal_texture != null: material.set_shader_parameter("normal_tex", source.normal_texture)
950			if material.shader == KIT_SHADER:
951				material.set_shader_parameter("gain", gain)
952				material.set_shader_parameter("snow_bias", snow_bias)
953			mesh.surface_set_material(surface, material)
954		_kit_cache[key] = mesh
955		return mesh

  `apply_scene_look(false)` swaps in `field_environment()` (`game/game_manager.gd:6620-6630`),
  built from `base_environment()`: ACES tonemap, SSAO, SSIL, glow, fog, adjustment
  (`game/game_manager.gd:6536-6562`, `game/game_manager.gd:6588-6603`).

  (`entities/ground_hazard.gd:1-2`, `extends Node3D`). It has no `.tscn`; it is made in
  code by `GameManager.spawn_hazard()` (`game/game_manager.gd:794-805`), called from
  `Molotov._land()` with `fuse` 0 and `lasting = fire_time` (`entities/molotov.gd:66-67`).

  (`entities/ground_hazard.gd:14-15`), counted down by physics `delta` in
  `_physics_process()` only while `game.simulation_active()` is true
  (`entities/ground_hazard.gd:62-78`, `game/game_manager.gd:386-387`); the node frees
  itself when `lasting <= 0` (`entities/ground_hazard.gd:78`). Fire duration
  comes from `fire_time` 3.0 (`game/enemy_attacks.gd:34`), zeroed when the thrower is
  silenced (`entities/enemy.gd:1200`). Non-fire users of the same class
  (`lasting` 0): `entities/enemy.gd:1443`, `entities/boss.gd:347`.

  (`world/base_map.gd:90`), loaded from `res://art/kit/base_crate.glb`
  (`KIT` pattern at `world/base_map.gd:57`; file listed in `art/kit/`).
  Material origin: `TerraceDressing.kit_mesh()` takes each glb surface's baked
  `BaseMaterial3D` albedo/normal textures into a `ShaderMaterial` using
  `res://world/kit_piece.gdshader` (`world/terrace_dressing.gd:38`,
  `world/terrace_dressing.gd:933-955`); `BaseMap._place_kit()` then overrides each surface
  with a `ShaderMaterial` on `res://world/base_kit_see_through.gdshader`, copying
  `albedo_tex`/`normal_tex`, possibly shared per room (`world/base_map.gd:58`,
  `world/base_map.gd:1744-1766`). Baked textures: `art/kit/base_crate_base_crate_body.png`,
  `..._label.png` and their `_normal.png` files.

  Godot `--headless --path . --script res://tests/<file> --fixed-fps <fps>`, logs to
  `logs/<name>_<fps>fps.log`, and fails on a non-zero exit or a `SHADER ERROR`/`SCRIPT ERROR`
  line (`scripts/run-test.sh:2`, `scripts/run-test.sh:10-14`). Suites are `extends SceneTree`
  and `quit(1 if failures else 0)` (`tests/test_new_enemies.gd:1`, `tests/test_new_enemies.gd:59`).
  - Existing thrower/Molotov/GroundHazard regression (`tests/test_new_enemies.gd:227-247`):
    `bash scripts/run-test.sh test_new_enemies.gd 60`
  - R3 timing tests, per `CHANGE-BRIEF.md:104-106`, at three fixed render rates:
    `bash scripts/run-test.sh <fire_test>.gd 30`
    `bash scripts/run-test.sh <fire_test>.gd 60`
    `bash scripts/run-test.sh <fire_test>.gd 144`
  - Long suites: `TEST_TIMEOUT=600 bash scripts/run-test.sh <test>.gd 60` (`scripts/run-test.sh:5`, `scripts/run-test.sh:11`).

## Current change

@CHANGE-BRIEF.md

## Ownership

- Files in `shaders/` (`res://shaders/`) are hand-written by the human and are never
  edited by an agent. This includes the planned `res://shaders/burning_bottle_fire.gdshader`
  and `res://shaders/cargo_panel.gdshader` (`CHANGE-BRIEF.md:44`, `CHANGE-BRIEF.md:234`).
  An agent does not create, edit, reformat or "fix" them; report a problem instead.

## Out of scope

- Gameplay: damage formulas, the bottle's direct hit, fire tick damage, who gets hurt,
  `GroundHazard.TICK` 0.5, first-tick timing, the 3.0 s fire life, radius 1.3,
  the 0.6 s bottle flight, and silence setting `fire_time` to 0.
- Collision, movement, input, the enemy state machine, windup/recovery, and the
  expected values in existing tests.
- The existing Decal scorch: its texture, colour, projection and lifetime stay as they are;
  the new flame mesh sits beside it and only draws flames.

  state. It never writes game state, deals damage or uses its own timer to decide
  the hazard's life.
- Calibration settings (Linear tonemap, post-processing off) are for one-off capture runs only:
  copy the Environment, restore it afterwards, and never save them as game defaults.
- No changes to `project.godot` renderer/driver settings or to the existing
  `world/*.gdshader` files.

## Project context

  the test wrapper runs `../Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64_console.exe` (`scripts/run-test.sh:8`).

- Renderer: `project.godot` sets no `rendering_method`; it only sets the Windows
  driver `rendering_device/driver.windows="d3d12"` (`project.godot:27`). A runtime
  check recorded in `CHANGE-BRIEF.md:27-31` read `renderer=forward_plus`, `driver=d3d12`.
  The visual suites in `tests/run_all.ps1:70` force `--rendering-method gl_compatibility`.
- Main scene: `res://game/main.tscn` (`project.godot:15`), a single `PixelDisplay` node
  (`game/main.tscn:5-6`) whose script renders the 3D world in a `SubViewport`
  and creates the `GameManager` (`game/pixel_display.gd:22`, `game/pixel_display.gd:44`).
- Field environment: created in `game/game_manager.gd:6500-6509`; in the field
  `apply_scene_look(false)` swaps in `field_environment()` (`game/game_manager.gd:6620-6630`),
  built from `base_environment()`: ACES tonemap, SSAO, SSIL, glow, fog, adjustment
  (`game/game_manager.gd:6536-6562`, `game/game_manager.gd:6588-6603`).
- How the shaded object is drawn: the burning-bottle fire is a `GroundHazard`
  (`entities/ground_hazard.gd:1-2`, `extends Node3D`). It has no `.tscn`; it is made in
  code by `GameManager.spawn_hazard()` (`game/game_manager.gd:794-805`), called from
  `Molotov._land()` with `fuse` 0 and `lasting = fire_time` (`entities/molotov.gd:66-67`).
  Today the fire is only a `Decal` with a code-made circle texture and emission
  texture (`entities/ground_hazard.gd:31-39`, `entities/ground_hazard.gd:52-60`).
- State that drives the effect: `fuse` and `lasting` on `GroundHazard`
  (`entities/ground_hazard.gd:14-15`), counted down by physics `delta` in
  `_physics_process()` only while `game.simulation_active()` is true
  (`entities/ground_hazard.gd:62-78`, `game/game_manager.gd:386-387`); the node frees
  itself when `lasting <= 0` (`entities/ground_hazard.gd:78`). Fire duration
  comes from `fire_time` 3.0 (`game/enemy_attacks.gd:34`), zeroed when the thrower is
  silenced (`entities/enemy.gd:1200`). Non-fire users of the same class
  (`lasting` 0): `entities/enemy.gd:1443`, `entities/boss.gd:347`.

  (`KIT` pattern at `world/base_map.gd:57`; file listed in `art/kit/`).
  Material origin: `TerraceDressing.kit_mesh()` takes each glb surface's baked
  `BaseMaterial3D` albedo/normal textures into a `ShaderMaterial` using
  `res://world/kit_piece.gdshader` (`world/terrace_dressing.gd:38`,
  `world/terrace_dressing.gd:933-955`); `BaseMap._place_kit()` then overrides each surface
  with a `ShaderMaterial` on `res://world/base_kit_see_through.gdshader`, copying
  `albedo_tex`/`normal_tex`, possibly shared per room (`world/base_map.gd:58`,
  `world/base_map.gd:1744-1766`). Baked textures: `art/kit/base_crate_base_crate_body.png`,
  `..._label.png` and their `_normal.png` files.
  The planned review fixture is `res://tests/material_review.tscn` (`CHANGE-BRIEF.md:225`; does not exist yet).
- Tests: every test goes through `scripts/run-test.sh <test-file.gd> <fps>`, which runs
  Godot `--headless --path . --script res://tests/<file> --fixed-fps <fps>`, logs to
  `logs/<name>_<fps>fps.log`, and fails on a non-zero exit or a `SHADER ERROR`/`SCRIPT ERROR`
  line (`scripts/run-test.sh:2`, `scripts/run-test.sh:10-14`). Suites are `extends SceneTree`
  and `quit(1 if failures else 0)` (`tests/test_new_enemies.gd:1`, `tests/test_new_enemies.gd:59`).
